description: Common aartis in Devanagari with transliteration and meaning. Traditional texts; regional versions vary.

items.text:
ॐ जय जगदीश हरे, स्वामी जय जगदीश हरे।
भक्त जनों के संकट, दास जनों के संकट, क्षण में दूर करे॥
ॐ जय जगदीश हरे॥
items.transliteration:
om jaya jagadīśa hare, svāmī jaya jagadīśa hare
bhakta janoṁ ke saṅkaṭa, dāsa janoṁ ke saṅkaṭa, kṣaṇa meṁ dūra kare
om jaya jagadīśa hare

translations.en: Victory to the Lord of the universe, O Master. The troubles of devotees, the troubles of servants, are removed in an instant.
translations.hi: हे जगत के स्वामी, आपकी जय हो। भक्तों और सेवकों के संकट आप क्षण भर में दूर कर देते हैं।

items.summary_1line: The best-known aarti in North India
items.summary_2to3line: It praises the Lord of the universe and asks him to clear the troubles of those who come to him.
items.bodh_3to4line: Sung at the end of almost any puja, especially in the evening. It is the default aarti when no specific deity is being worshipped.

items.text:
ॐ जय शिव ओंकारा, स्वामी जय शिव ओंकारा।
ब्रह्मा विष्णु सदाशिव, अर्द्धांगी धारा॥
ॐ जय शिव ओंकारा॥
items.transliteration:
om jaya śiva oṁkārā, svāmī jaya śiva oṁkārā
brahmā viṣṇu sadāśiva, arddhāṅgī dhārā
om jaya śiva oṁkārā

translations.en: Victory to Shiva, who is Om. Brahma, Vishnu and Sadashiva, and the one who holds the half-body (Parvati).
translations.hi: ॐ के स्वरूप शिव की जय। ब्रह्मा, विष्णु, सदाशिव तथा अर्धांगिनी पार्वती सहित आपकी जय हो।

items.summary_1line: The main aarti of Lord Shiva
items.summary_2to3line: It names Shiva as Om itself, and honours his place alongside Brahma and Vishnu and his consort.
items.bodh_3to4line: Sung on Shivratri, during Monday fasts, and at the end of any Shiva puja or rudrabhishek.

items.text:
ॐ जय लक्ष्मी माता, मैया जय लक्ष्मी माता।
तुमको निशिदिन सेवत, हर विष्णु विधाता॥
ॐ जय लक्ष्मी माता॥
items.transliteration:
om jaya lakṣmī mātā, maiyā jaya lakṣmī mātā
tumako niśidina sevata, hara viṣṇu vidhātā
om jaya lakṣmī mātā

translations.en: Victory to Mother Lakshmi. Day and night Shiva, Vishnu and the Creator serve you.
translations.hi: हे माता लक्ष्मी, आपकी जय हो। शिव, विष्णु और विधाता दिन-रात आपकी सेवा करते हैं।

items.summary_1line: The aarti of the goddess of prosperity
items.summary_2to3line: It honours Lakshmi as the one served by the great gods themselves, and asks for her steady presence.
items.bodh_3to4line: Sung on Diwali, on Fridays, and during Lakshmi puja. Often sung after the Lakshmi puja steps are complete.

items.text:
जय गणेश जय गणेश जय गणेश देवा।
माता जाकी पार्वती पिता महादेवा॥
एक दन्त दयावन्त चार भुजा धारी।
माथे सिन्दूर सोहे मूसे की सवारी॥
items.transliteration:
jaya gaṇeśa jaya gaṇeśa jaya gaṇeśa devā
mātā jākī pārvatī pitā mahādevā
eka danta dayāvanta cāra bhujā dhārī
māthe sindūra sohe mūse kī savārī

translations.en: Victory to Ganesha, whose mother is Parvati and father Mahadeva. One-tusked, kind, four-armed, vermilion on his brow, riding a mouse.
translations.hi: गणेश जी की जय हो, जिनकी माता पार्वती और पिता महादेव हैं। एकदंत, दयालु, चार भुजाधारी, मस्तक पर सिंदूर और मूषक की सवारी।

items.summary_1line: The aarti of the remover of obstacles
items.summary_2to3line: It describes Ganesha plainly — his parents, his one tusk, his four arms, his mouse — and asks him to be present.
items.bodh_3to4line: Sung first, before any other aarti, because Ganesha is invoked at the start of every undertaking.

items.text:
जय अम्बे गौरी, मैया जय श्यामा गौरी।
तुमको निशिदिन ध्यावत, हरि ब्रह्मा शिवरी॥
जय अम्बे गौरी॥
items.transliteration:
jaya ambe gaurī, maiyā jaya śyāmā gaurī
tumako niśidina dhyāvata, hari brahmā śivarī
jaya ambe gaurī

translations.en: Victory to Ambe Gauri, Mother, to Shyama Gauri. Vishnu, Brahma and Shiva meditate on you day and night.
translations.hi: हे अम्बे गौरी, माता, आपकी जय हो। हरि, ब्रह्मा और शिव दिन-रात आपका ध्यान करते हैं।

items.summary_1line: The aarti of the Mother goddess
items.summary_2to3line: It praises the goddess as the one the great gods themselves meditate upon, under both her bright and dark forms.
items.bodh_3to4line: Sung during Navratri, on Durga puja days, and at the end of a Devi puja.

items.text:
ॐ जय सरस्वती माता, मैया जय सरस्वती माता।
सद्गुण वैभव शालिनी, त्रिभुवन विख्याता॥
ॐ जय सरस्वती माता॥
items.transliteration:
om jaya sarasvatī mātā, maiyā jaya sarasvatī mātā
sadguṇa vaibhava śālinī, tribhuvana vikhyātā
om jaya sarasvatī mātā

translations.en: Victory to Mother Saraswati, endowed with virtue and splendour, renowned through the three worlds.
translations.hi: हे माता सरस्वती, आपकी जय हो। सद्गुणों और वैभव से युक्त, तीनों लोकों में विख्यात।

items.summary_2to3line: It praises Saraswati as the one famed through all three worlds for virtue and grace, and asks for her blessing on speech and study.
items.bodh_3to4line: Sung on Vasant Panchami, before exams or a new course of study, and in schools and music rooms.

items.text:
आरती कीजै हनुमान लला की।
दुष्ट दलन रघुनाथ कला की॥
जाके बल से गिरिवर कांपे।
रोग दोष जाके निकट न झांके॥
items.transliteration:
āratī kījai hanumāna lalā kī
duṣṭa dalana raghunātha kalā kī
jāke bala se girivara kāṁpe
roga doṣa jāke nikaṭa na jhāṁke

translations.en: Perform the aarti of Hanuman, the destroyer of the wicked, the art of Raghunatha. Mountains tremble at his strength; disease and fault do not come near him.
translations.hi: हनुमान जी की आरती कीजिए, जो दुष्टों का नाश करने वाले और रघुनाथ की कला हैं। जिनके बल से पर्वत कांपते हैं और रोग-दोष पास नहीं आते।

items.summary_2to3line: It praises Hanuman's strength and his service to Rama, and asks that illness and ill fortune keep their distance.
items.bodh_3to4line: Sung on Tuesdays and Saturdays, and at the end of a Hanuman Chalisa reading.

items.text:
जय तुलसी माता, जय तुलसी माता।
जय श्री तुलसी माता, जय तुलसी माता॥
items.transliteration:
jaya tulasī mātā, jaya tulasī mātā
jaya śrī tulasī mātā, jaya tulasī mātā

translations.en: Victory to Mother Tulsi, victory to Mother Tulsi.
translations.hi: हे तुलसी माता, आपकी जय हो।

items.summary_1line: The short aarti sung to the Tulsi plant
items.summary_2to3line: It greets the Tulsi plant as a mother and asks for her blessing on the household.
items.bodh_3to4line: Sung while watering or circling the Tulsi plant, usually in the morning or at dusk.
